title: Auth/API key 401/429 debugging scratchpad
content:
Context:
- Intermittent 401 and 429 errors reported by a small subset of customers (hosted API).
- Errors started ~2026-03-10 22:00 UTC after a rollout of a token-rotation helper in the proxy layer.
- Repro rate low: ~5% of requests to /v1/generate returned 401; 429s occur in spikes immediately after bursts.

Symptoms observed:
- 401 patterns: immediate 401 response with body: '{"error":{"message":"Unauthorized","type":"invalid_api_key"}}'
- 429 patterns: response body: '{"error":{"message":"Rate limit exceeded"}}' and headers include Retry-After and X-RateLimit-* in some cases.
- Affected customers mostly on dedicated and some high-traffic hosted customers.

Commands / reproductions tried (local + curl):
- Basic request that fails reproducibly for cust A (token replaced with <REDACTED>):
  curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"redwood-13b","input":"hello"}'

  -> HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
  Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 09:14:22 GMT
  Content-Type: application/json
  Content-Length: 92

  {"error":{"message":"Unauthorized","type":"invalid_api_key"}}

- Same request with a different key (works): 200 + tokens returned.
- Replaced the key with one from the same customer (rotated, different key id) -> request succeeds.
- Observed one case where key worked for several minutes then started returning 401.

- 429 reproduction (artificial bursts):
  for i in {1..120}; do \
    curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -X POST \
    https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -d '{"model":"embed-2","input":"x"}' &
  done

  -> observed many 200s then a block of 429 responses. Example headers when 429 returned:
  HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
  Retry-After: 30
  X-RateLimit-Limit: 60
  X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
  X-RateLimit-Reset: 170... (epoch)

Observations from logs (proxy + auth-service + rate-limiter):
- Proxy logs show token id mapping and decision tree: if key marked revoked -> immediate 401.
- For some affected requests token verification path shows: token looked up in cache (redis) -> not found -> call to auth-service -> auth-service returns 401 (invalid) -> proxy logs 401.
- In auth-service traces for a particular key id: auth-service queried k/v store (postgres) and returned 200 for key status "active". But proxy still treated as invalid in same minute.
- Found occasional race where token-rotation job sets key status to 'revoked' then quickly to 'active' again (classic double-write race + cache TTL mismatch).
- Rate-limiter: per-key token bucket implemented in redis with lua script. On heavy bursts the script latencies spike; sometimes script returns ERR and code falls back to defensive 429s.

Error snippets and timestamps:
- 2026-03-10T22:01:12Z proxy: tokenId=kj12sx: cache MISS -> auth-call start
- 2026-03-10T22:01:12Z auth: tokenId=kj12sx -> db status=active (SELECT 1)
- 2026-03-10T22:01:12Z proxy: tokenId=kj12sx -> allowed=false -> 401 to client

- Rate limiter error (redis lua):
  2026-03-11T08:59:03Z rl: script_eval ERR Error running script (call to f_...): NOSCRIPT No matching script.
  -> fallback increments in-memory counters -> many simultaneous requests see 0 remaining -> 429 sent.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Token rotation race: when rotating keys we briefly mark new/old keys and update cache TTLs; if propagation order wrong, proxy cache and auth DB disagree -> transient 401s. Evidence: keys that fail then succeed after small delay; rotation job logs show quick successive status flips.
2) Cache inconsistency TTL: Redis cache TTL for token metadata too long/short relative to PG updates; when backfill/repair runs, entries can be inconsistent.
3) Rate-limiter script eviction: redis script cache eviction (NOSCRIPT) under node restarts or failovers causes rate-limiter fallback to error path returning 429.
4) Client-side: some SDKs may be reusing stale embedded keys (less likely given server logs).

Immediate mitigation actions taken:
- Rolled back token-rotation helper to previous safe version (2026-03-10 23:00 UTC). Monitoring shows 401 occurrences dropped to baseline.
- Put guard in proxy: if auth-service returns "active" but proxy would reject due to cache mismatch, consider short-circuit recheck (sync call) as temporary fix.
- Added NOSCRIPT handling for rate-limiter: automatically re-load lua script on NOSCRIPT rather than fallback-to-error.

Planned next steps / TODOs:
- [ ] Add stronger invariants to token-rotation job: write-order guarantees and post-write cache invalidation. (Owner: Aisha)
- [ ] Increase visibility: emit token-change events to infra-logs and trace id linking (Owner: Michael).
- [ ] Harden rate-limiter: ensure lua script SHA persisted and reloaded on reconnects; add metrics for lua script misses. (Owner: Oliver).
- [ ] Add canary traffic for token rotation job (limit to 1% of keys for first hour).
- [ ] Create regression test that simulates rotate+burst to reproduce race in CI.

Notes to self:
- Watch for patterns where 401s correlate with specific region proxies (us-west-2). Could be redis cluster partitioning.
- Check cloud provider maintenance windows around 2026-03-10 21:55-22:15 UTC.
- Follow up with customer success for impacted customers: provide incident writeup and timeline after fix.

Quick links (internal):
- rotation job: GH:dotorg/infra-scripts/tree/token-rotate-helper (PR linked: GH:...#987)
- auth-service schema: confluence/?pageid=auth-schema
- infra dashboard: Grafana -> Auth -> TokenVerifications

Scratch observations (informal):
- Felt guilty about deploying rotation helper without canary. Note to future self: small canaries only.
- If we keep getting NOSCRIPT -> might need to pin redis version or reduce ephemeral restarts.

End of scratchpad.
